card.problem: The gap family and h2 bet on the open or the whole session, so their P&L hinged on a few big gap days (concentration 1.00-3.14). Breaks of yesterday's high or low that happen inside the session, on days that opened inside yesterday's range, have not been tested at all.
card.motivation: Lesson from h1.2-h1.2.5: continuation existed but was carried by a few large-gap days and failed concentration and DSR. Removing gap days and requiring the break to happen during the session isolates a different event. A 1 ATR take cap stops any single trend day from carrying the net, which is the check every predecessor failed. The quiet-open clause reuses the gap family's own finding that gaps under ~0.3% behaved as noise.
card.approach: On days that open within 0.3% of yesterday's close, go long on the first 1-minute close above yesterday's high (short below yesterday's low) after 09:45, with a 0.5 ATR stop, a 1 ATR take and flat at 15:15.
card.plan: Features ph = prev_day(high), pl = prev_day(low), g = gap_pct, m = minute_of_day, atr(days 14). Entry long: close > ph and abs(g) < p.g and m >= 30; short: close < pl and abs(g) < p.g and m >= 30; max_per_day 1. Exit stop_atr 0.5, take_atr 1.0, time 15:15. CPCV over g in [0.002, 0.003, 0.005]; demo gate.
card.mechanism: Stop-loss and breakout buy-stop orders cluster just beyond the prior day's extremes (Osler 2005, stop-loss cascades in FX). When an in-session move reaches them, the triggered market orders push price further, and late breakout traders follow. The stop holders pay because their orders are placed for risk control, not price.
card.rule: long: close > prev_day high and abs(gap_pct) < p.g and minute_of_day >= 30; short mirror at prev_day low; stop 0.5 ATR, take 1 ATR, exit 15:15

g.source: h1.2 post-mortem (earlier gap run): gaps of 0.3% or less lost money as a continuation signal, so it marks 'no informative gap'; grid 0.002/0.003/0.005

kill: best 5 days carry >= 50% of net despite the 1 ATR take cap
dropping the abs(gap_pct) clause does not hurt (ablation), i.e. it is just the gap family again

cpcv.note: N=10 k=2 9 paths, 0% positive, SR sd 0.10

synthetic_exit.note: AR(1) phi=1.0000; exit beats 91% of 400 synthetic exits

replies.body: h6 round 1: spec written for prev-range-break. It only trades on days whose gap is under g. From 09:45 it goes long on a close above yesterday's high, or short on a close below yesterday's low. It trades at most once a day and exits on a 0.5 ATR stop, a 1 ATR take or at 15:15. g is 0.003, with a grid of 0.002, 0.003 and 0.005. Expressions can't read the raw close, so the close is sma(close, 1), which is the same value. One difference from the card: if price was already beyond yesterday's high or low before 09:45, the spec enters at 09:45. That trade isn't a fresh break. Sizing follows the reference spec, since the card gives none. It passes the spec loader.

h6 round 1: FAIL (gate a13f4a4b)
The report doesn't say whether this was the demo gate, so I'm not stating which thresholds applied. 11 of 15 checks failed, with 394 bets and net -3.6L.
- passed: probe (clean), determinism (identical), min_bets (394 vs ≥50), beats_refs (-0.22 vs "SR > refs", as printed), synthetic_exit (0.91 vs ≥0.5, a flag check).

  - cpcv: -0.17 vs >0.0. The typical backtest path lost money. The share of money-making paths isn't in the report.

  - pbo: 0.77 vs ≤0.1. A 77% chance the chosen setting is overfit.
  - exposure_null: 0.34 vs ≥0.95. The report doesn't show the null it compares against.
  - costs: 0.68 vs ≥3.0. Gross profit is less than costs.
  - p_failure: 0.96 vs ≤0.05.
  - concentration: 1.00 vs <0.5. No HHI value is shown. A value of 1.00 means a few days account for all of the net.
  - drawdown: 0.30 vs ≤0.2. Over the limit. The time-under-water value isn't shown.
  - robustness: -0.47 vs >0.
  - ablation: only 1 of 3 clauses hurt when removed, so two clauses aren't earning their place.
- patch: patch 1 of 4 was allowed, so it isn't a hard stop. The ablation result suggests removing or simplifying one of the unhelpful clauses. Costs and concentration are also open. It must be argued from training folds only. The report doesn't name which clauses.
